## The verbs (full argument forms)

```
hm intent status --json
hm intent question add <id> --claim --status <open|confirmed|wrong> [--text --observed-at [--locator <path:A-B>]]
hm intent question observe <id> --relation <confirms|supersedes|contradicts> --text --observed-at [--claim] [--locator <path:A-B>]
hm intent question resolve <id> --status --claim
hm intent metric record <id> --value --observed-at --evidence
hm intent new <id> --title --statement --scope --metric [--out-of-scope] [--from-proposal --candidates <N> [--declined <title>]…]
hm intent <approve|activate|drop|reopen> <id>
hm intent close <id> --observed <met|missed|no_data> --note
hm intent show <id> --json
```

Prefix each with `uv run --with $HOME/harness-maker/.worktrees/world-intent-closed-loop` as every other mandated call
in this harness does. `--observed-at` is a timezone-aware ISO-8601 timestamp; `supersedes`
needs `--claim`; `close` needs both `--observed` and `--note`.

reports `stale_evidence` when that text changed (approval checks never read cited files).

## The rule for every write

1. Work out the verb and its arguments from what the operator said; read `status` first when
   an id is ambiguous.
2. Ask with `request_user_input`, showing the exact arguments
   you are about to pass.
3. On an affirmative answer, run the write once with those arguments and show the CLI's
   `changed:` line.
4. Otherwise — on any other answer or no answer — write nothing. Do not retry, rephrase or infer consent.

## Creation: mandatory deep interview and quality review

Apply to direct creation, accepted proposals, and drafts requested by another workflow stage.
Interview the intent creator before `new`; a one-line request or candidate selection is not a completed interview.
Reuse explicit answers from this conversation; ask the creator to correct the synthesis and probe remaining gaps.
Use `request_user_input_async` when available, or ask in chat and wait; use `request_user_input` only where allowed.
Ask one to three adaptive multiple-choice questions per round, with concrete, distinct proposals.
Put the recommended option first, label it, and briefly explain why; always offer a final free-text Other path.
Use the question tool's built-in Other input when present; otherwise add Other explicitly. Do not lead with free-text-only questions.
Cover: problem and affected users; desired observable change and why now; evidence and assumptions;
success measure, baseline, target and measurement method; scope, exclusions and tradeoffs;
decision owner, feedback timing and what happens on success, failure or missing data.
When artifacts or workflow are affected, cover discoverability, authoritative records, placement rationale,
existing conventions and compatibility. Do not impose a folder migration on unrelated intents.
Probe vague goals with a concrete success example and a counterexample that would not count as success.
Separate creator answers, observed evidence and agent suggestions; never manufacture targets or claim a baseline.
If no existing metric fits, discuss a suitable definition with the creator; never silently add one or use an unrelated metric.
Stop asking when the creator has resolved the material gaps; preserve implementation questions for the SPEC.
Without answers, keep a conversational draft and explain the missing decisions; do not run `new`.

Before writing, proactively critique clarity, outcome relevance, measurability, scope coherence, evidence,
decision/feedback ownership, and overlap with existing or rejected intents. Fix wording; interview for missing decisions.
Show the proposed statement, scope/exclusions, metric and evidence, responsibilities, and remaining questions.
Flag proxy metrics that can pass without the intended outcome; require complementary completion evidence where needed.
Material gaps prevent creation until answered; implementation details may remain explicitly deferred.
Obtain the creator's confirmation of this concrete draft under the write rule, then create it as `proposed`.
Populate the Markdown body's Problem, Proposed outcome, Affected users and systems, Constraints and Open questions
from the confirmed draft, preserving the CLI-owned frontmatter; do not leave unexplained empty sections.
Read back the record and status, check references and consistency with the confirmed draft, and report any error.
On quality-review requests or substantive revisions, apply this critique without waiting to be asked about each gap;
reuse existing answers and interview only for changed or missing decisions. Never reopen or alter terminal records.

## Proposing intents (only when the operator asks what to do next / where the gaps are)

1. Run `hm intent status --json` — read-only, LLM-free. On `state: invalid` print the error and stop;
   on `not_filled_in` say the purpose and metrics are unwritten and stop.
2. Open with a **measure first** block: every metric whose `reason` is `never_measured` or
   `stale_definition`, with its `how_measured` — those are gaps in evidence, not in the code.
   For the ones with `measure: true`, run `hm intent metric measure --all --dry-run` and show
   the table; the record call is `hm intent metric measure --all`, gated by
   "The rule for every write" above (ask once, run once on yes, otherwise write nothing).
3. Read the codebase against the measured metrics' `gap` and propose **at most three**
   candidates, unranked, each with `title / statement / scope / out_of_scope / metric / evidence /
   overlaps-with`. A candidate for an unmeasured metric carries
   `evidence: none — statement only`. `overlaps-with` names any intent (any state,
   especially `closed` + `observed:
   missed`) or any `rejected[]` entry the candidate resembles — never silently re-propose it.
4. Then ask about each candidate in turn with `request_user_input` (yes / no), and
   answer every candidate before the first write: the declined titles go into every accepted
   record's `rejected[]`.
5. Then, once per accepted candidate, show the exact arguments and run
   `hm intent new <ID> … --from-proposal --candidates <N> --declined "<title>"…`
   only after its deep interview and quality review (`N` = candidates shown; one `--declined` per no).
   Nothing else persists a candidate.
6. The record is `proposed`; the proposer never runs `approve` — that stamp is the operator's.

intent never changes, and the autopilot gate reads the approval you record. Whether the work
serves the intent is the operator's judgment and `/hm:review`'s Step 3.3, not this skill's.

# intent-layer

Translate matching prose into one `hm intent` verb; creation requires the deep interview and quality review below.
Workflow stages may load feedback without a separate mention; intent changes still require consent.

**Read freely, write only on an answer.** `hm intent status --json` is read-only, LLM-free and
free to run whenever the operator asks where things stand. Mutation verbs write only after consent.

Distinct nonblank `owners` roles trigger an advisory at approval, never a block.
`approved_by` is an unverified git config string; real separation requires
CODEOWNERS + branch protection. Empty or identical roles stay silent.

One intent may serve multiple SPECs (1:N); the record is `intent/<ID>.md`.
`hm intent migrate --json` preserves record body bytes, approvals and historical clocks;
Run it before the first canonical write. Reads accept legacy files without rewriting them.

Workflow feedback: read and follow `references/workflow-feedback.md` at workflow triggers.

## The verbs (full argument forms)

```
hm intent status --json
hm intent question add <id> --claim --status <open|confirmed|wrong> [--text --observed-at [--locator <path:A-B>]]
hm intent question observe <id> --relation <confirms|supersedes|contradicts> --text --observed-at [--claim] [--locator <path:A-B>]
hm intent question resolve <id> --status --claim
hm intent metric record <id> --value --observed-at --evidence
hm intent new <id> --title --statement --scope --metric [--out-of-scope] [--from-proposal --candidates <N> [--declined <title>]…]
hm intent <approve|activate|drop|reopen> <id>
hm intent close <id> --observed <met|missed|no_data> --note
hm intent show <id> --json
```

Prefix each with `uv run --with $HOME/harness-maker/.worktrees/world-intent-closed-loop` as every other mandated call
in this harness does. `--observed-at` is a timezone-aware ISO-8601 timestamp; `supersedes`
needs `--claim`; `close` needs both `--observed` and `--note`.
`--locator <path:A-B>` cites at most 40 lines of this checkout by content; `status --json` then
reports `stale_evidence` when that text changed (approval checks never read cited files).

## The rule for every write

1. Work out the verb and its arguments from what the operator said; read `status` first when
   an id is ambiguous.
2. Ask with `request_user_input`, showing the exact arguments
   you are about to pass.
3. On an affirmative answer, run the write once with those arguments and show the CLI's
   `changed:` line.
4. Otherwise — on any other answer or no answer — write nothing. Do not retry, rephrase or infer consent.

## Creation: mandatory deep interview and quality review

Apply to direct creation, accepted proposals, and drafts requested by another workflow stage.
Interview the intent creator before `new`; a one-line request or candidate selection is not a completed interview.
Reuse explicit answers from this conversation; ask the creator to correct the synthesis and probe remaining gaps.
Use `request_user_input_async` when available, or ask in chat and wait; use `request_user_input` only where allowed.
Ask one to three adaptive multiple-choice questions per round, with concrete, distinct proposals.
Put the recommended option first, label it, and briefly explain why; always offer a final free-text Other path.
Use the question tool's built-in Other input when present; otherwise add Other explicitly. Do not lead with free-text-only questions.
Cover: problem and affected users; desired observable change and why now; evidence and assumptions;
success measure, baseline, target and measurement method; scope, exclusions and tradeoffs;
decision owner, feedback timing and what happens on success, failure or missing data.
When artifacts or workflow are affected, cover discoverability, authoritative records, placement rationale,
existing conventions and compatibility. Do not impose a folder migration on unrelated intents.
Probe vague goals with a concrete success example and a counterexample that would not count as success.
Separate creator answers, observed evidence and agent suggestions; never manufacture targets or claim a baseline.
If no existing metric fits, discuss a suitable definition with the creator; never silently add one or use an unrelated metric.
Stop asking when the creator has resolved the material gaps; preserve implementation questions for the SPEC.
Without answers, keep a conversational draft and explain the missing decisions; do not run `new`.

Before writing, proactively critique clarity, outcome relevance, measurability, scope coherence, evidence,
decision/feedback ownership, and overlap with existing or rejected intents. Fix wording; interview for missing decisions.
Show the proposed statement, scope/exclusions, metric and evidence, responsibilities, and remaining questions.
Flag proxy metrics that can pass without the intended outcome; require complementary completion evidence where needed.
Material gaps prevent creation until answered; implementation details may remain explicitly deferred.
Obtain the creator's confirmation of this concrete draft under the write rule, then create it as `proposed`.
Populate the Markdown body's Problem, Proposed outcome, Affected users and systems, Constraints and Open questions
from the confirmed draft, preserving the CLI-owned frontmatter; do not leave unexplained empty sections.
Read back the record and status, check references and consistency with the confirmed draft, and report any error.
On quality-review requests or substantive revisions, apply this critique without waiting to be asked about each gap;
reuse existing answers and interview only for changed or missing decisions. Never reopen or alter terminal records.

## Proposing intents (only when the operator asks what to do next / where the gaps are)

1. Run `hm intent status --json` — read-only, LLM-free. On `state: invalid` print the error and stop;
   on `not_filled_in` say the purpose and metrics are unwritten and stop.
2. Open with a **measure first** block: every metric whose `reason` is `never_measured` or
   `stale_definition`, with its `how_measured` — those are gaps in evidence, not in the code.
   For the ones with `measure: true`, run `hm intent metric measure --all --dry-run` and show
   the table; the record call is `hm intent metric measure --all`, gated by
   "The rule for every write" above (ask once, run once on yes, otherwise write nothing).
3. Read the codebase against the measured metrics' `gap` and propose **at most three**
   candidates, unranked, each with `title / statement / scope / out_of_scope / metric / evidence /
   overlaps-with`. A candidate for an unmeasured metric carries
   `evidence: none — statement only`. `overlaps-with` names any intent (any state,
   especially `closed` + `observed:
   missed`) or any `rejected[]` entry the candidate resembles — never silently re-propose it.
4. Then ask about each candidate in turn with `request_user_input` (yes / no), and
   answer every candidate before the first write: the declined titles go into every accepted
   record's `rejected[]`.
5. Then, once per accepted candidate, show the exact arguments and run
   `hm intent new <ID> … --from-proposal --candidates <N> --declined "<title>"…`
   only after its deep interview and quality review (`N` = candidates shown; one `--declined` per no).
   Nothing else persists a candidate.
6. The record is `proposed`; the proposer never runs `approve` — that stamp is the operator's.

What the harness guarantees is narrow: the record changes only through these verbs, a terminal
intent never changes, and the autopilot gate reads the approval you record. Whether the work
serves the intent is the operator's judgment and `/hm:review`'s Step 3.3, not this skill's.
